methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $152M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Humanoid is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Artem Sokolov that has raised $152M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics), supplemented by a broader set of nine private peers and one public comparable (277810.KQ).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a typical 2.0x multiplier to the $152M capital raised as a valuation proxy, implying $304M. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of four robotics peers at $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed stage) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The peer set reflects meaningful stage heterogeneity—three comps are Series B and one Seed—which introduces variance but provides market-informed reference points for the subsector.

The triangulated analysis yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a low bound of $258M and high bound of $2.0B. The wide range reflects tension between the stage-progression method, which assumes earlier-stage discounting, and the peer-median approach, which draws from more mature peers. Key uncertainties include the degree to which Humanoid's capital efficiency and technology differentiation warrant premium or discount relative to the peer set, and whether the heterogeneous stage mix of comparables adequately anchors Series A value.
